aws.c2b.connect.contact_flow_logs.description: Reads the CONTACTFLOW_LOGS instance attribute of each Amazon Connect instance and flags the instance when its value is anything other than the string 'true'. Without contact flow logs, the execution path of customer calls and chats through flows is not recorded in CloudWatch, so fraud, misrouting or abuse of IVR flows cannot be reconstructed.
aws.c2b.connect.contact_flow_logs.pass_when: The CONTACTFLOW_LOGS attribute value is exactly 'true'.
aws.c2b.connect.contact_flow_logs.fail_when: The CONTACTFLOW_LOGS attribute value is 'false' or any value other than 'true'.

aws.c2b.datasync.task_log_group.description: Inspects the DescribeTask detail of each AWS DataSync task and fails the task when no CloudWatchLogGroupArn is configured; the log level is deliberately not considered. A task without a log group leaves no CloudWatch record of which files were transferred, skipped or failed verification, hiding data exfiltration or integrity problems in bulk transfers.
aws.c2b.datasync.task_log_group.pass_when: The task detail contains a non-empty CloudWatchLogGroupArn.
aws.c2b.datasync.task_log_group.fail_when: CloudWatchLogGroupArn is omitted or empty in the task detail.

aws.c2b.datasync.task_logging_level.description: Stricter DataSync logging variant: a DataSync task fails unless it both has a CloudWatchLogGroupArn and Options.LogLevel set to BASIC or TRANSFER. A log group with LogLevel OFF (or unset) still produces no transfer logs, so failed or tampered file copies and unexpected destinations go unrecorded.
aws.c2b.datasync.task_logging_level.pass_when: A log group ARN is set and Options.LogLevel is BASIC or TRANSFER.
aws.c2b.datasync.task_logging_level.fail_when: The log group ARN is missing, or Options.LogLevel is OFF, missing or any other value.

aws.c2b.dax.encryption_at_rest.description: Reads SSEDescription.Status of each DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster, treating an omitted SSEDescription as DISABLED, and fails any cluster whose status is not ENABLED. Cached DynamoDB items on DAX node storage are then unencrypted at rest, and because SSE can only be chosen at cluster creation the cluster must be rebuilt to fix it.
aws.c2b.dax.encryption_at_rest.fail_when: SSEDescription.Status is DISABLED, any value other than ENABLED, or SSEDescription is omitted.

aws.c2b.dax.encryption_in_transit.description: Reads ClusterEndpointEncryptionType of each DAX cluster (omission treated as the API default NONE) and fails the cluster unless it is TLS. A plaintext DAX endpoint exposes cached DynamoDB items and requests to anyone able to sniff traffic inside the VPC.
aws.c2b.dax.encryption_in_transit.fail_when: ClusterEndpointEncryptionType is NONE, omitted, or any value other than TLS.

aws.c2b.dax.multi_az.description: Collects the AvailabilityZone of every node in a DAX cluster and fails the cluster when the distinct set of zones has fewer than two members (including a cluster with no listed nodes). A single-AZ DAX cluster loses its whole cache layer during an AZ outage, pushing all read load back onto DynamoDB or breaking applications that depend on it.
aws.c2b.dax.multi_az.pass_when: Cluster nodes are spread over at least two distinct Availability Zones.
aws.c2b.dax.multi_az.fail_when: All nodes are in one Availability Zone or the node list is empty/omitted.

aws.c2b.directconnect.connection_redunda.description: Region-scope check over all collected Direct Connect connections: it fails the region when there is only one connection or when all connections terminate at the same Direct Connect location. A single connection or location is a single point of failure for hybrid connectivity to on-premises networks.
aws.c2b.directconnect.connection_redunda.pass_when: The region has at least two connections and they use at least two distinct locations.
aws.c2b.directconnect.connection_redunda.fail_when: The region has exactly one connection, or all connections share one location.
aws.c2b.directconnect.connection_redunda.not_applicable_when: The region has no Direct Connect connections.

aws.c2b.directconnect.virtual_interface_.description: Groups every Direct Connect virtual interface by the virtual private gateway or Direct Connect gateway it attaches to and fails the region when any gateway has fewer than two VIFs or all of its VIFs ride on the same physical connection. Distinct connections are counted, so two VIFs on one connection still fail; such a gateway loses on-premises reachability when that connection drops.
aws.c2b.directconnect.virtual_interface_.pass_when: Every gateway has at least two virtual interfaces spread over at least two distinct connections.
aws.c2b.directconnect.virtual_interface_.fail_when: At least one gateway has a single virtual interface or all its interfaces use the same connection.
aws.c2b.directconnect.virtual_interface_.not_applicable_when: No virtual interface in the region is attached to a virtual or Direct Connect gateway.

aws.c2b.directoryservice.certificate_not.description: For each AWS Directory Service directory that has registered LDAPS/client certificates, computes calendar days (date difference) between each certificate's ExpiryDateTime and the snapshot date and fails if any certificate has fewer than 90 calendar days left (Steampipe boundary). An expired directory certificate breaks LDAPS/smart-card authentication or forces fallback to unencrypted LDAP.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.certificate_not.pass_when: Every registered certificate has 90 or more calendar days until expiry.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.certificate_not.fail_when: Any registered certificate expires in fewer than 90 calendar days (or is already expired).
aws.c2b.directoryservice.certificate_not.not_applicable_when: The directory is Simple AD (no LDAPS certificate support) or has no registered certificates.

aws.c2b.directoryservice.ldap_certificat.description: Prowler-boundary variant: for each directory with registered certificates, takes the floor of (ExpiryDateTime - now) in whole days and fails if any certificate has 90 or fewer days remaining. This catches LDAPS certificates about to expire, which would interrupt secure LDAP binds from applications and users.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.ldap_certificat.pass_when: Every registered certificate has more than 90 full days remaining.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.ldap_certificat.fail_when: Any registered certificate has 90 or fewer full days remaining (including expired ones).
aws.c2b.directoryservice.ldap_certificat.not_applicable_when: The directory is Simple AD or has no registered certificates.

aws.c2b.directoryservice.log_forwarding.description: Checks the ListLogSubscriptions result for each Directory Service directory and fails when the list is empty. Without a log subscription, domain controller security event logs (logons, account changes) are not forwarded to CloudWatch Logs, so brute-force and privilege abuse inside the managed AD are not centrally monitored.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.log_forwarding.pass_when: At least one log subscription exists for the directory.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.log_forwarding.fail_when: The collected log subscription list is empty.

aws.c2b.directoryservice.manual_snapshot.description: Reads GetSnapshotLimits for each directory and fails when ManualSnapshotsLimitReached is true or when ManualSnapshotsLimit minus ManualSnapshotsCurrentCount is 2 or less. Running out of manual snapshot quota blocks taking a restore point before risky changes, weakening recovery of the directory.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.manual_snapshot.pass_when: The limit is not reached and more than two manual snapshots of quota remain.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.manual_snapshot.fail_when: ManualSnapshotsLimitReached is true or only two or fewer manual snapshot slots remain.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.manual_snapshot.not_applicable_when: GetSnapshotLimits returned a documented not-found/unsupported marker for the directory (e.g. AD Connector).

aws.c2b.directoryservice.radius_mfa_enab.description: Fails a Directory Service directory whose RadiusStatus is not 'Completed', including directories that report no RadiusStatus at all. Without RADIUS-backed MFA, directory credentials alone grant access to WorkSpaces, the AWS console via AD and other integrated apps, so stolen passwords are directly usable.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.radius_mfa_enab.fail_when: RadiusStatus is missing, 'Failed', 'Creating' or any value other than 'Completed'.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.radius_mfa_enab.not_applicable_when: The directory Type is SimpleAD or SharedMicrosoftAD.

aws.c2b.directoryservice.radius_ms_chapv.description: For directories that have RadiusSettings configured, reads RadiusSettings.AuthenticationProtocol and fails unless it is MS-CHAPv2. Weaker RADIUS protocols such as PAP, CHAP or MS-CHAPv1 send or protect the user's credential with obsolete schemes between the directory and the RADIUS server.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.radius_ms_chapv.fail_when: AuthenticationProtocol is PAP, CHAP, MS-CHAPv1 or any value other than MS-CHAPv2.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.radius_ms_chapv.not_applicable_when: The directory has no RadiusSettings (no RADIUS server configured).

aws.c2b.directoryservice.shared_accounts.description: Lists the SharedAccountId values from DescribeSharedDirectories for each directory; a directory that is not shared with any account passes, and a directory shared with one or more accounts is returned as MANUAL with those account IDs for a trust review (no trusted-account list is configured, so the check never emits FAIL). Sharing a managed AD with an untrusted account lets that account join instances to the domain and authenticate against it.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.shared_accounts.pass_when: The directory is not shared with any other account.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.shared_accounts.fail_when: Never FAIL; a directory shared with any account yields MANUAL for review of the listed accounts.

aws.c2b.directoryservice.sns_notificatio.description: Fails a Directory Service directory when DescribeEventTopics returns no registered SNS topic. Without an event topic, nobody is notified when the directory's status changes to Impaired or Inoperable, delaying response to domain controller outages.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.sns_notificatio.pass_when: At least one SNS event topic is registered for the directory.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.sns_notificatio.fail_when: The collected event topic list is empty.
aws.c2b.directoryservice.sns_notificatio.not_applicable_when: The directory Type is SharedMicrosoftAD (DescribeEventTopics is unsupported).

aws.c2b.dlm.ebs_snapshot_policy_with_sna.description: Region-scope check: in a region that holds at least one EBS snapshot, it fails unless at least one Data Lifecycle Manager policy has a PolicyType beginning with EBS_SNAPSHOT (the policy state is not checked). Without such a policy, snapshot creation and retention are manual, risking missing backups or unbounded stale snapshots.
aws.c2b.dlm.ebs_snapshot_policy_with_sna.pass_when: The region has a DLM policy whose PolicyType starts with EBS_SNAPSHOT.
aws.c2b.dlm.ebs_snapshot_policy_with_sna.fail_when: The region has EBS snapshots but no DLM policy of an EBS_SNAPSHOT type.
aws.c2b.dlm.ebs_snapshot_policy_with_sna.not_applicable_when: The region has no EBS snapshots.

aws.c2b.dlm.policy_exists_with_snapshots.description: Region-scope Prowler variant: a region containing EBS snapshots fails when it has no Data Lifecycle Manager lifecycle policy of any type (EBS_SNAPSHOT, IMAGE or EVENT policies all count). This flags regions where snapshot backups exist but no automated lifecycle governance at all is configured.
aws.c2b.dlm.policy_exists_with_snapshots.pass_when: At least one DLM lifecycle policy of any type exists in the region.
aws.c2b.dlm.policy_exists_with_snapshots.fail_when: The region has EBS snapshots and zero DLM lifecycle policies.
aws.c2b.dlm.policy_exists_with_snapshots.not_applicable_when: The region has no EBS snapshots.

aws.c2b.dms.certificate_not_expired.description: Compares each AWS DMS certificate's ValidToDate with the start of the snapshot day minus one second and fails the certificate when it is already past that cutoff. Expired certificates attached to DMS endpoints cause SSL verification failures or push operators to downgrade endpoint SslMode, weakening replication transport security.
aws.c2b.dms.certificate_not_expired.pass_when: ValidToDate is on or after the start of the snapshot day minus one second.
aws.c2b.dms.certificate_not_expired.fail_when: ValidToDate is earlier than that cutoff (certificate expired).

aws.c2b.dms.endpoint_ssl.description: Reads SslMode on every AWS DMS source/target endpoint and fails only when it is explicitly 'none'; an omitted SslMode passes, matching both upstream rules. An endpoint with SslMode none replicates database rows and credentials between DMS and the database in cleartext.
aws.c2b.dms.endpoint_ssl.pass_when: SslMode is any value except the exact string 'none', including when omitted.

aws.c2b.dms.mongodb_auth.description: For DMS endpoints whose EngineName is mongodb, reads MongoDbSettings.AuthType (an omitted value defaults to 'no') and fails when it is 'no'. A MongoDB endpoint without authentication means DMS connects to (and the database accepts) unauthenticated sessions, so anyone reaching the MongoDB port can read or alter the replicated data.
aws.c2b.dms.mongodb_auth.pass_when: MongoDbSettings.AuthType is set to a value other than 'no' (e.g. password).
aws.c2b.dms.mongodb_auth.fail_when: MongoDbSettings.AuthType is 'no' or MongoDbSettings/AuthType is omitted.
aws.c2b.dms.mongodb_auth.not_applicable_when: The endpoint EngineName is not mongodb.

aws.c2b.dms.neptune_iam_auth.description: For DMS endpoints whose EngineName is neptune, reads NeptuneSettings.IamAuthEnabled (omitted inside collected settings means false) and fails when it is not true. Without IAM authorization, DMS writes to the Neptune cluster without SigV4-signed, IAM-scoped requests, so access to the graph target is not governed or audited by IAM.
aws.c2b.dms.neptune_iam_auth.fail_when: NeptuneSettings.IamAuthEnabled is false or omitted from the collected NeptuneSettings.
aws.c2b.dms.neptune_iam_auth.not_applicable_when: The endpoint EngineName is not neptune.

aws.c2b.dms.public_instance_open_sg.description: For a DMS replication instance with PubliclyAccessible true, resolves its VpcSecurityGroups and fails when any attached security group has an ingress rule from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 that is all-protocols (-1) or carries a port range. A public replication instance reachable from the whole Internet exposes the host that holds source/target database credentials and in-flight data.
aws.c2b.dms.public_instance_open_sg.pass_when: The instance is not publicly accessible, has no security groups, or none of its groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.
aws.c2b.dms.public_instance_open_sg.fail_when: The instance is publicly accessible and at least one attached security group allows ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.

aws.c2b.dms.redis_tls.description: For DMS endpoints whose EngineName is redis, reads RedisSettings.SslSecurityProtocol (omitted means the documented default ssl-encryption) and fails when it is anything else, typically plaintext. A plaintext Redis target lets anyone on the network path read or inject the data DMS writes into the cache.
aws.c2b.dms.redis_tls.fail_when: SslSecurityProtocol is plaintext or any value other than ssl-encryption.
aws.c2b.dms.redis_tls.not_applicable_when: The endpoint EngineName is not redis.

aws.c2b.dms.task_source_logging.description: Parses the ReplicationTaskSettings JSON of each DMS replication task and fails unless Logging.EnableLogging is true and both the SOURCE_CAPTURE and SOURCE_UNLOAD log components have severity LOGGER_SEVERITY_DEFAULT, DEBUG or DETAILED_DEBUG. Missing source-side logs hide CDC capture and full-load read failures and make data-loss or tampering investigations on the source database impossible.
aws.c2b.dms.task_source_logging.pass_when: Logging is enabled and SOURCE_CAPTURE and SOURCE_UNLOAD each log at DEFAULT, DEBUG or DETAILED_DEBUG severity.
aws.c2b.dms.task_source_logging.fail_when: Logging is disabled, or SOURCE_CAPTURE or SOURCE_UNLOAD is missing or set to a lower severity such as WARNING or ERROR.

aws.c2b.dms.task_target_logging.description: Parses the ReplicationTaskSettings JSON of each DMS replication task and fails unless Logging.EnableLogging is true and both the TARGET_APPLY and TARGET_LOAD components log at LOGGER_SEVERITY_DEFAULT, DEBUG or DETAILED_DEBUG. Without target-side logs, failed or partial writes into the destination database during full load and CDC apply go unnoticed.
aws.c2b.dms.task_target_logging.pass_when: Logging is enabled and TARGET_APPLY and TARGET_LOAD each log at DEFAULT, DEBUG or DETAILED_DEBUG severity.
aws.c2b.dms.task_target_logging.fail_when: Logging is disabled, or TARGET_APPLY or TARGET_LOAD is missing or set to a lower severity.

aws.c2b.docdb.cluster_tls_required.description: For DB clusters with Engine docdb, reads the 'tls' value from the cluster parameter group parameters and fails when it is 'disabled' or 'enabled' (the latter still permits TLS 1.0/1.1). Clients can then connect to DocumentDB without TLS or with deprecated protocol versions, exposing queries and credentials in transit.
aws.c2b.docdb.cluster_tls_required.pass_when: The tls parameter is tls1.2+, tls1.3+, fips-140-3 or another value except disabled/enabled.
aws.c2b.docdb.cluster_tls_required.not_applicable_when: The cluster Engine is not docdb.

aws.c2b.docdb.instance_storage_encrypted.description: Instance-level DocumentDB check: for RDS-API DB instances with Engine docdb, fails when StorageEncrypted is not true. Unencrypted instance storage leaves documents, indexes and logs readable from underlying volumes, snapshots and replicas.
aws.c2b.docdb.instance_storage_encrypted.pass_when: StorageEncrypted is true on the docdb instance.
aws.c2b.docdb.instance_storage_encrypted.fail_when: StorageEncrypted is false on the docdb instance.
aws.c2b.docdb.instance_storage_encrypted.not_applicable_when: The DB instance Engine is not docdb.

aws.c2b.docdb.snapshot_not_public_prowle.description: For DB cluster snapshots of Engine docdb, reads the DescribeDBClusterSnapshotAttributes result and fails when the value 'all' appears in any attribute's AttributeValues, even alongside specific account IDs. A snapshot restorable by 'all' can be copied and restored by any AWS account, leaking the entire DocumentDB dataset.
aws.c2b.docdb.snapshot_not_public_prowle.not_applicable_when: The cluster snapshot Engine is not docdb.

aws.c2b.docdb.snapshot_restore_not_all_e.description: For DocumentDB cluster snapshots, checks the restore attribute for membership of the public principal all, even when account IDs are also present. Missing, malformed or denied restore attributes remain UNKNOWN.
aws.c2b.docdb.snapshot_restore_not_all_e.pass_when: No restore attribute value includes all.
aws.c2b.docdb.snapshot_restore_not_all_e.fail_when: The restore attribute includes all, alone or alongside account IDs.
aws.c2b.docdb.snapshot_restore_not_all_e.not_applicable_when: The snapshot Engine is not docdb.

aws.c2b.documentdb.backup_retention_7.description: For DB clusters with Engine docdb, reads BackupRetentionPeriod and fails when it is below 7 days. Short retention limits point-in-time recovery after accidental deletes, ransomware-style corruption or late-detected data tampering.
aws.c2b.documentdb.backup_retention_7.not_applicable_when: The cluster Engine is not docdb.

aws.c2b.documentdb.cluster_log_exports.description: For docdb-engine clusters, reads EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports (omitted means none) and fails unless both 'audit' and 'profiler' are exported to CloudWatch Logs. Without the audit export, authentication and DDL/DML events are not retained outside the cluster, and without profiler logs abusive or slow operations cannot be traced.
aws.c2b.documentdb.cluster_log_exports.pass_when: EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports contains both audit and profiler.
aws.c2b.documentdb.cluster_log_exports.fail_when: Either audit or profiler (or both) is missing from EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports.
aws.c2b.documentdb.cluster_log_exports.not_applicable_when: The cluster Engine is not docdb.

aws.c2b.documentdb.deletion_protection.description: For docdb-engine clusters, fails when the cluster's DeletionProtection flag is not true. Without it, a single DeleteDBCluster call by a compromised or careless principal destroys the cluster and its automated backups.
aws.c2b.documentdb.deletion_protection.not_applicable_when: The cluster Engine is not docdb.

aws.c2b.documentdb.multi_az.description: For docdb-engine clusters, fails when the cluster-level MultiAZ attribute is not true, i.e. the cluster has no replica instance in another Availability Zone. An AZ outage then makes the DocumentDB cluster unavailable until a new instance is provisioned.
aws.c2b.documentdb.multi_az.not_applicable_when: The cluster Engine is not docdb.

aws.c2b.documentdb.storage_encrypted.description: Cluster-level DocumentDB encryption check: for docdb-engine clusters, fails when StorageEncrypted is not true. An unencrypted cluster volume exposes all documents and its snapshots to anyone who obtains storage-level or snapshot access, and encryption can only be added by restoring an encrypted copy.
aws.c2b.documentdb.storage_encrypted.pass_when: StorageEncrypted is true on the cluster.
aws.c2b.documentdb.storage_encrypted.fail_when: StorageEncrypted is false on the cluster.
aws.c2b.documentdb.storage_encrypted.not_applicable_when: The cluster Engine is not docdb.

aws.c2b.drs.region_has_job.description: Uses the complete DRS DescribeSourceServers inventory to evaluate configured source-server replication states; historical job count is not service enablement or recovery readiness. Remediation: Restore continuous replication for impaired configured source servers; validate required protection scope, drills, launch settings and RTO with workload owners.
aws.c2b.drs.region_has_job.pass_when: Every configured source server reports CONTINUOUS replication.
aws.c2b.drs.region_has_job.fail_when: A configured source reports STOPPED, STALLED or DISCONNECTED; denied, missing or intermediate states are UNKNOWN.
aws.c2b.drs.region_has_job.not_applicable_when: The complete region inventory has no configured source servers, absent an approved protection scope.

aws.c2b.dynamodb.capacity_autoscaling.description: For DynamoDB tables in PROVISIONED billing mode (an omitted BillingModeSummary counts as PROVISIONED), looks up Application Auto Scaling targets with ServiceNamespace dynamodb and ResourceId table/<name> and fails unless both ReadCapacityUnits and WriteCapacityUnits scalable dimensions are registered; on-demand tables pass. Fixed provisioned capacity causes throttling under load spikes, which is an availability risk for dependent applications.
aws.c2b.dynamodb.capacity_autoscaling.pass_when: The table is PAY_PER_REQUEST, or both table read and write capacity scalable targets exist.
aws.c2b.dynamodb.capacity_autoscaling.fail_when: The table is provisioned and lacks a read or a write capacity scalable target.

aws.c2b.dynamodb.policy_not_cross_accoun.description: Evaluates the DynamoDB table resource policy with Prowler's is_policy_public using the audited account and cross-account disallowed: an Allow statement whose principal is a wildcard or any AWS principal outside the audited account fails, unless a restrictive account, organization or private-IP condition applies. Such a policy lets other AWS accounts (or everyone) read or modify table data directly.
aws.c2b.dynamodb.policy_not_cross_accoun.pass_when: No Allow statement grants an external or wildcard principal without a restricting condition.
aws.c2b.dynamodb.policy_not_cross_accoun.fail_when: An Allow statement grants a wildcard principal or a principal from another account without a restrictive condition.
aws.c2b.dynamodb.policy_not_cross_accoun.not_applicable_when: The table has no resource policy.

aws.c2b.dynamodb.sse_kms.description: Reads SSEDescription.SSEType of each DynamoDB table and fails unless it is KMS; an omitted SSEDescription means the default AWS-owned key and fails. With the AWS-owned key, encryption cannot be audited in CloudTrail or revoked through key policy, so access to table data is not separately controllable.
aws.c2b.dynamodb.sse_kms.pass_when: SSEType is KMS (AWS managed or customer managed key).
aws.c2b.dynamodb.sse_kms.fail_when: SSEDescription is omitted (AWS-owned key) or SSEType is not KMS.

aws.c2b.dynamodb.table_in_backup_selecti.description: Searches every AWS Backup plan selection: the DynamoDB table passes if a selection's Resources contains its ARN, '*' or arn:<partition>:dynamodb:*:*:table/*, or if any ListOfTags ConditionKey equals one of the table's tag keys (tag values are not compared). Otherwise it fails, meaning the table is not covered by any centrally managed backup schedule.
aws.c2b.dynamodb.table_in_backup_selecti.pass_when: A backup selection references the table ARN or a matching wildcard, or uses a tag condition key the table carries.
aws.c2b.dynamodb.table_in_backup_selecti.fail_when: No backup selection matches the table by ARN, wildcard or tag key.

aws.c2b.dynamodb.table_in_backup_selecti.description: Prowler variant that only matches backup selection Resources: the DynamoDB table fails unless some AWS Backup plan selection lists its exact ARN, arn:<partition>:dynamodb:*:*:table/* or '*'. Tag-based selections are not considered, so tables protected only through tag conditions also fail here.
aws.c2b.dynamodb.table_in_backup_selecti.pass_when: A backup selection's Resources contains the table ARN, the dynamodb table wildcard or '*'.
aws.c2b.dynamodb.table_in_backup_selecti.fail_when: No backup selection's Resources matches the table.

aws.c2b.dynamodb.table_protected_resourc.description: Checks the AWS Backup ListProtectedResources inventory and fails the DynamoDB table unless an entry has its exact ResourceArn with ResourceType DynamoDB. Unlike selection-based checks, this requires that a recovery point has actually been created, so a table with no backups at all is reported.
aws.c2b.dynamodb.table_protected_resourc.pass_when: The table ARN appears as a protected resource of type DynamoDB.
aws.c2b.dynamodb.table_protected_resourc.fail_when: The table ARN is not listed as a DynamoDB protected resource.

aws.c2b.ecr.latest_image_no_medium_plus_.description: For a scan-on-push ECR repository, selects the latest pushed scannable image and reads scan findings for that exact digest. A complete scan with valid aggregate counts and completion time is required to establish absence of MEDIUM, HIGH or CRITICAL findings. Remediation: Rebuild and push a patched image, then confirm a complete exact-digest scan with no MEDIUM, HIGH or CRITICAL findings.
aws.c2b.ecr.latest_image_no_medium_plus_.pass_when: The selected exact-digest scan is COMPLETE with valid counts, observed completion time and zero MEDIUM, HIGH and CRITICAL findings; valid historical DescribeImages snapshots are supported.
aws.c2b.ecr.latest_image_no_medium_plus_.fail_when: The selected scan is FAILED or has a positive MEDIUM, HIGH or CRITICAL count; pending, denied, missing, malformed or incomplete facts are UNKNOWN.
aws.c2b.ecr.latest_image_no_medium_plus_.not_applicable_when: Scan on push is disabled or there are no scannable images.

aws.c2b.ecr.registry_automated_scanning.description: For a registry with repositories, checks one automated SCAN_ON_PUSH or CONTINUOUS_SCAN rule whose own WILDCARD repository filter is *. A complete ENHANCED configuration with no rules defaults to continuous scanning for all repositories. This is configuration evidence, not proof that scans completed.
aws.c2b.ecr.registry_automated_scanning.pass_when: One automated rule itself has a * WILDCARD filter, or a complete ENHANCED configuration has an explicit empty rules list.
aws.c2b.ecr.registry_automated_scanning.fail_when: No automated rule covers every repository, or complete BASIC configuration has no rules.
aws.c2b.ecr.registry_automated_scanning.not_applicable_when: The registry in the Region holds no repositories.

aws.c2b.ecr.registry_enhanced_scanning.description: Region-scope check of the ECR registry scanning configuration: when the registry holds at least one repository, it fails unless scanType is ENHANCED (omitted counts as BASIC). Basic scanning only covers OS packages at push time, while enhanced Amazon Inspector scanning continuously covers OS and language packages, so BASIC leaves newly disclosed vulnerabilities in stored images undetected.
aws.c2b.ecr.registry_enhanced_scanning.not_applicable_when: The registry in the region holds no repositories.

aws.c2b.ecr.repository_not_public.description: Evaluates the ECR repository policy with Prowler's is_policy_public for the audited account: it fails when an Allow statement has a public principal ('*' or arn:aws:iam::*:root) and no restrictive account, organization or private-IP condition. A public repository policy lets any AWS identity pull (or, depending on actions, push) container images, leaking code and secrets baked into images or enabling supply-chain tampering.
aws.c2b.ecr.repository_not_public.pass_when: No Allow statement grants a public principal without a restrictive condition.
aws.c2b.ecr.repository_not_public.fail_when: An Allow statement grants '*' or arn:aws:iam::*:root without a restrictive condition.
aws.c2b.ecr.repository_not_public.not_applicable_when: The repository has no repository policy.

aws.c2b.ecr.repository_policy_no_wildcar.description: Steampipe variant: scans the ECR repository policy for any Allow statement with actions whose Principal is '*' or whose Principal.AWS includes '*', ignoring all conditions. Even conditioned wildcard grants are flagged, because any condition error turns the repository into one any AWS principal can access.
aws.c2b.ecr.repository_policy_no_wildcar.pass_when: The repository has no policy or no Allow statement with a nonempty Action and a wildcard AWS principal.
aws.c2b.ecr.repository_policy_no_wildcar.fail_when: An Allow statement with a nonempty Action names '*' as an AWS principal, regardless of conditions.

aws.c2b.ecr.repository_policy_prohibit_p.description: aws-perimeter variant: fails the ECR repository when an Allow statement's principal is exactly the wildcard and none of the keys aws:SourceOwner, SourceAccount, PrincipalOrgID, PrincipalAccount, PrincipalArn or SourceArn constrains it with a non-wildcard StringEquals/StringLike/ArnEquals/ArnLike value. Such statements make the repository usable by principals outside the organization perimeter.
evaluated: Policy.policyText (Statement[].Effect/Principal/Condition keys aws:sourceowner, aws:sourceaccount, aws:principalorgid, aws:principalaccount, aws:principalarn, aws:sourcearn)
aws.c2b.ecr.repository_policy_prohibit_p.pass_when: Every wildcard-principal Allow statement is restricted by one of the perimeter condition keys.
aws.c2b.ecr.repository_policy_prohibit_p.fail_when: Any Allow statement with a wildcard principal lacks an effective perimeter condition.
aws.c2b.ecr.repository_policy_prohibit_p.not_applicable_when: The repository has no repository policy.

aws.c2b.ecs.all_containers_logging.description: Universal logging check on ECS task definitions: every container definition must carry a logConfiguration with a non-empty logDriver, and the task definition fails if any single container (for example a sidecar) lacks one. Containers without a log driver emit no stdout/stderr to CloudWatch or another sink, leaving gaps in evidence for intrusions in that container.
aws.c2b.ecs.all_containers_logging.pass_when: All container definitions have a logConfiguration with a logDriver.
aws.c2b.ecs.all_containers_logging.fail_when: At least one container definition has no logConfiguration or an empty logDriver.

aws.c2b.ecs.awsvpc_service_no_public_ip.description: Joins each ECS service to its task definition and, only when the task definition's networkMode is awsvpc, fails if networkConfiguration.awsvpcConfiguration.assignPublicIp is anything other than DISABLED (omitted counts as DISABLED). Tasks with public IPs are directly addressable from the Internet, bypassing load balancers and exposing container ports to scanning and exploitation.
aws.c2b.ecs.awsvpc_service_no_public_ip.pass_when: For an awsvpc task definition, assignPublicIp is DISABLED or omitted (defaulted to DISABLED).
aws.c2b.ecs.awsvpc_service_no_public_ip.fail_when: For an awsvpc task definition, assignPublicIp has any value other than DISABLED.
aws.c2b.ecs.awsvpc_service_no_public_ip.not_applicable_when: The service's task definition uses a network mode other than awsvpc (bridge, host, none).

aws.c2b.ecs.cluster_has_active_services.description: Reads activeServicesCount of each ECS cluster and fails when it is zero or less. Clusters with no services are typically abandoned infrastructure that still carries IAM roles, capacity providers or container instances, widening the attack surface and inventory drift.

aws.c2b.ecs.cluster_has_registered_insta.description: Reads registeredContainerInstancesCount of each ECS cluster and fails when it equals zero, reproducing the Steampipe rule (Fargate-only clusters therefore fail as well). It is an inventory-hygiene signal for empty EC2-backed clusters rather than a direct security weakness.
aws.c2b.ecs.cluster_has_registered_insta.pass_when: At least one container instance is registered to the cluster.

aws.c2b.ecs.cluster_instance_volumes_enc.description: For ECS clusters with registered container instances, follows each container instance to its EC2 instance's BlockDeviceMappings and the referenced EBS volumes, failing when any of those volumes has Encrypted false. Unencrypted container-host volumes expose images, container writable layers, logs and any secrets written to disk via snapshots or detached volumes.
aws.c2b.ecs.cluster_instance_volumes_enc.pass_when: Every EBS volume attached to the cluster's container instances is encrypted.
aws.c2b.ecs.cluster_instance_volumes_enc.fail_when: Any attached EBS volume of a container instance has Encrypted false.
aws.c2b.ecs.cluster_instance_volumes_enc.not_applicable_when: The cluster has zero registered container instances.

aws.c2b.ecs.container_insights.description: Prowler variant: reads the cluster settings list and fails unless some containerInsights setting has value 'enabled' or 'enhanced'; a cluster with no settings at all fails. Without Container Insights there are no per-task CPU, memory and network metrics, making resource abuse such as cryptomining or denial-of-service hard to spot.
aws.c2b.ecs.container_insights.pass_when: A containerInsights setting is enabled or enhanced.
aws.c2b.ecs.container_insights.fail_when: There is no containerInsights setting or its value is disabled.

aws.c2b.ecs.container_insights_setting.description: Checks an ECS cluster's collected settings list for containerInsights. An empty list or missing entry fails; enabled and enhanced pass. Missing or denied cluster detail is UNKNOWN.
aws.c2b.ecs.container_insights_setting.pass_when: At least one containerInsights setting is present and every such value is enabled or enhanced.
aws.c2b.ecs.container_insights_setting.fail_when: The collected settings list is empty, lacks containerInsights, or contains a disabled or unrecognized value.

aws.c2b.ecs.container_instance_agents_co.description: For ECS clusters with registered instances, inspects the cluster's container instances and fails if any instance with status ACTIVE has agentConnected false. A disconnected ECS agent means the host no longer receives task placements, stops reporting state and may run stale or unmanaged containers outside orchestration control.
aws.c2b.ecs.container_instance_agents_co.pass_when: Every ACTIVE container instance has agentConnected true.
aws.c2b.ecs.container_instance_agents_co.fail_when: At least one ACTIVE container instance reports agentConnected false.
aws.c2b.ecs.container_instance_agents_co.not_applicable_when: The cluster has zero registered container instances.

aws.c2b.ecs.container_instance_in_vpc.description: For each ECS container instance backed by an EC2 instance (ID starting with i-), looks up the EC2 instance and fails when it has no VpcId. An instance outside a VPC (legacy EC2-Classic) cannot use security groups, NACLs or flow logs in the modern way and has no private network isolation.
aws.c2b.ecs.container_instance_in_vpc.pass_when: The backing EC2 instance has a VpcId.
aws.c2b.ecs.container_instance_in_vpc.fail_when: The backing EC2 instance has no VpcId.
aws.c2b.ecs.container_instance_in_vpc.not_applicable_when: The container instance is not an EC2 instance (e.g. ECS Anywhere mi- managed instance).

aws.c2b.ecs.fargate_latest_platform.description: For ECS services with launchType FARGATE, passes platformVersion LATEST or the current documented version (1.4.0 for Linux, 1.0.0 for Windows families) and fails any other pinned version. Older Fargate platform versions miss kernel and runtime security patches as well as features such as ephemeral storage encryption.
aws.c2b.ecs.fargate_latest_platform.pass_when: platformVersion is LATEST, or 1.4.0 on Linux, or 1.0.0 on a Windows platform family.
aws.c2b.ecs.fargate_latest_platform.fail_when: platformVersion is any other value for the service's platform family (e.g. 1.3.0 on Linux).
aws.c2b.ecs.fargate_latest_platform.not_applicable_when: The service launchType is not FARGATE (EC2, EXTERNAL, or capacity provider strategy without launchType).

aws.c2b.ecs.host_network_root_user.description: For ECS task definitions with networkMode host, fails when any non-privileged container has no user, user 'root' or UID 0 (user part before ':'); task definitions in other network modes pass. Root containers sharing the host network namespace can bind privileged ports, sniff host traffic and reach instance metadata, easing escape to the container host.
aws.c2b.ecs.host_network_root_user.pass_when: networkMode is not host, or every non-privileged container sets a non-root user.
aws.c2b.ecs.host_network_root_user.fail_when: networkMode is host and some non-privileged container has user empty, root or 0.

aws.c2b.ecs.logging_non_blocking.description: For ECS task definitions with at least one container that has a log driver, fails when a container's logConfiguration.options.mode is set to anything other than non-blocking, or when the mode is unset and the account's defaultLogDriverMode setting is not non-blocking. Blocking log delivery makes containers stall when the log destination is unavailable, turning a logging outage into an application outage.
aws.c2b.ecs.logging_non_blocking.pass_when: Every logged container uses mode non-blocking, explicitly or inherited from a non-blocking (or absent) account default.
aws.c2b.ecs.logging_non_blocking.fail_when: Some logged container uses mode blocking, or inherits a blocking defaultLogDriverMode account setting.
aws.c2b.ecs.logging_non_blocking.not_applicable_when: No container in the task definition has a log driver configured.

aws.c2b.ecs.no_credential_named_env_vars.description: Checks only the names (never values) of plaintext environment entries in every container definition and fails when any is AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or ECS_ENGINE_AUTH_DATA; names supplied via the secrets[] array are not flagged. Plain environment variables are visible to anyone with ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition, so long-lived AWS keys or registry auth stored there are easily stolen.
aws.c2b.ecs.no_credential_named_env_vars.pass_when: No container environment entry uses one of the three credential variable names.
aws.c2b.ecs.no_credential_named_env_vars.fail_when: Any container environment entry is named AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or ECS_ENGINE_AUTH_DATA.

aws.c2b.ecs.service_load_balancer_attach.description: Fails an ECS service whose loadBalancers list is empty. Services fronted by an Elastic Load Balancing target group get health-checked replacement of unhealthy tasks and traffic spread across tasks/AZs; without one, a failed task can keep serving errors and clients must reach tasks directly.
aws.c2b.ecs.service_load_balancer_attach.pass_when: The service has at least one load balancer/target group attached.
aws.c2b.ecs.service_load_balancer_attach.fail_when: The service's loadBalancers list is empty.

aws.c2b.ecs.service_no_public_ip.description: Prowler variant on ECS services: reads networkConfiguration.awsvpcConfiguration.assignPublicIp (omitted means DISABLED) and fails only when it is ENABLED, without checking the task definition network mode. Tasks launched with public IPs are reachable from the Internet on any port their security groups allow.
aws.c2b.ecs.service_no_public_ip.pass_when: assignPublicIp is any value except ENABLED, including an omitted awsvpc configuration (defaulted to DISABLED).
aws.c2b.ecs.service_no_public_ip.fail_when: assignPublicIp is exactly ENABLED on the service.

aws.c2b.ecs.task_set_no_public_ip.description: Applies the public-IP test to ECS task sets (used by external/CODE_DEPLOY deployment controllers): fails when the task set's networkConfiguration.awsvpcConfiguration.assignPublicIp is ENABLED. Task-set tasks with public IPs are exposed directly to the Internet even when the parent service looks private.
aws.c2b.ecs.task_set_no_public_ip.pass_when: assignPublicIp is any value except ENABLED, including an omitted awsvpc configuration (defaulted to DISABLED).
aws.c2b.ecs.task_set_no_public_ip.fail_when: assignPublicIp is exactly ENABLED on the task set.

aws.c2b.efs.access_point_root_directory.description: Per EFS access point, fails when RootDirectory.Path is '/'. An access point rooted at the file system root gives every client using it visibility over all directories, defeating the per-application directory isolation that access points are meant to enforce.
aws.c2b.efs.access_point_root_directory.pass_when: RootDirectory.Path is any string other than '/', including an empty string.

aws.c2b.efs.access_point_user_identity.description: Per EFS access point, fails when no PosixUser (Uid/Gid) is defined. Without an enforced POSIX identity, NFS clients act with whatever UID/GID they claim, including root, so file permissions on the share cannot be relied on.
aws.c2b.efs.access_point_user_identity.pass_when: The access point defines a PosixUser.
aws.c2b.efs.access_point_user_identity.fail_when: PosixUser is omitted on the access point.

aws.c2b.efs.access_points_no_root_direct.description: File-system-level aggregation: gathers all access points belonging to an EFS file system and fails the file system when any of them has RootDirectory.Path '/'. One root-path access point is enough to expose the entire file system tree to its clients.
aws.c2b.efs.access_points_no_root_direct.pass_when: No access point of the file system uses '/' as root directory.
aws.c2b.efs.access_points_no_root_direct.fail_when: At least one access point of the file system has RootDirectory.Path '/'.
aws.c2b.efs.access_points_no_root_direct.not_applicable_when: The file system has no access points.

aws.c2b.efs.access_points_posix_user.description: File-system-level aggregation: gathers all access points of an EFS file system and fails the file system when any access point lacks a PosixUser. A single access point without an enforced identity lets clients use arbitrary UIDs (including root) on that file system.
aws.c2b.efs.access_points_posix_user.pass_when: Every access point of the file system defines a PosixUser.
aws.c2b.efs.access_points_posix_user.fail_when: At least one access point of the file system has no PosixUser.
aws.c2b.efs.access_points_posix_user.not_applicable_when: The file system has no access points.

aws.c2b.efs.automatic_backups_enabled.description: Steampipe variant: reads the EFS file system's BackupPolicy.Status and fails unless it is exactly ENABLED, so ENABLING, DISABLING, DISABLED and a missing backup policy all fail. Without EFS automatic backups, deleted or encrypted-by-ransomware files have no AWS Backup recovery point.
aws.c2b.efs.automatic_backups_enabled.fail_when: BackupPolicy.Status is ENABLING, DISABLING, DISABLED, or no backup policy exists.

aws.c2b.efs.backup_not_disabled.description: Prowler variant: reads BackupPolicy.Status (a missing policy, PolicyNotFound, is treated as DISABLED) and fails only when it is DISABLED or DISABLING; ENABLED and ENABLING pass. It flags file systems whose automatic backups are turned off or being turned off, leaving no automatic recovery point.
aws.c2b.efs.backup_not_disabled.fail_when: BackupPolicy.Status is DISABLED or DISABLING, or no backup policy exists.

aws.c2b.efs.file_system_protected_resour.description: Checks the AWS Backup protected-resource inventory and fails an EFS file system unless its exact FileSystemArn is listed with ResourceType EFS. This means at least one recovery point exists for it in AWS Backup; otherwise there is no restorable backup after data loss.
aws.c2b.efs.file_system_protected_resour.pass_when: The file system ARN appears as an AWS Backup protected resource of type EFS.
aws.c2b.efs.file_system_protected_resour.fail_when: The file system ARN is not among the EFS protected resources.

aws.c2b.efs.mount_target_subnet_no_auto_.description: Joins an EFS mount target to its subnet and checks MapPublicIpOnLaunch, a subnet policy for future EC2 instances. It does not establish that the EFS mount target has a public IP or is reachable from the internet. Remediation: Use a subnet with MapPublicIpOnLaunch disabled if this source policy is required; inspect actual EFS routing and security groups separately.
aws.c2b.efs.mount_target_subnet_no_auto_.pass_when: The mount target subnet has MapPublicIpOnLaunch false.
aws.c2b.efs.mount_target_subnet_no_auto_.fail_when: The mount target subnet has MapPublicIpOnLaunch true; an unresolved subnet is UNKNOWN.

aws.c2b.efs.multi_az_mount_targets.description: Fails an EFS file system that is One Zone (an AvailabilityZoneId is present) and, for Regional file systems, fails when NumberOfMountTargets is 1 or less. Either way clients in other AZs have no local mount target, so an AZ failure makes the shared storage unreachable.
aws.c2b.efs.multi_az_mount_targets.pass_when: The file system has no AvailabilityZoneId (Regional) and more than one mount target.
aws.c2b.efs.multi_az_mount_targets.fail_when: The file system is One Zone (AvailabilityZoneId set) or has at most one mount target.

aws.c2b.efs.no_public_mount_targets.description: Checks whether any EFS mount target subnet has an effective default route to an internet gateway. The route alone does not prove a public EFS endpoint or inbound NFS reachability. Remediation: Place mount targets in subnets without an internet-gateway default route and verify NFS reachability separately.
aws.c2b.efs.no_public_mount_targets.pass_when: No mount target subnet has an effective 0.0.0.0/0 route to an internet gateway.
aws.c2b.efs.no_public_mount_targets.fail_when: At least one mount target subnet has that internet-gateway route; unresolved joins are UNKNOWN.

aws.c2b.efs.policy_enforces_ssl.description: Parses the EFS file system policy and passes only if some Deny statement with a '*' AWS principal and a non-empty Action carries Condition Bool aws:SecureTransport = false; a file system with no policy fails. Without this deny, NFS clients can mount and read/write the file system without TLS, exposing file contents on the network.
aws.c2b.efs.policy_enforces_ssl.pass_when: A Deny statement for principal '*' with an Action and Bool aws:SecureTransport false exists.
aws.c2b.efs.policy_enforces_ssl.fail_when: No such Deny statement exists, or the file system has no policy.

aws.c2b.efs.policy_no_wildcard_allow.description: Scans the EFS file system policy for Allow statements whose principal is '*' or AWS ['*'], ignoring any conditions; a file system without a policy passes. A wildcard Allow, even conditioned, means mount/write access is granted to any principal that satisfies (or circumvents) the condition, including principals in other accounts.
aws.c2b.efs.policy_no_wildcard_allow.pass_when: There is no policy or no Allow statement with a wildcard principal.
aws.c2b.efs.policy_no_wildcard_allow.fail_when: Any Allow statement names '*' as principal, regardless of conditions.

aws.c2b.efs.policy_not_open_to_vpc_clien.description: Checks relevant public Allow statements in an EFS file system policy for Bool elasticfilesystem:AccessedViaMountTarget=true. An unrelated Deny or private statement does not change this result. A missing policy fails because default anonymous mount-target access remains possible; this does not establish effective internet reachability.
aws.c2b.efs.policy_not_open_to_vpc_clien.pass_when: A policy exists and every relevant public Allow statement requires access through a mount target, or no relevant public Allow exists.
aws.c2b.efs.policy_not_open_to_vpc_clien.fail_when: No policy exists, or a relevant public Allow statement lacks the mount-target condition.

aws.c2b.efs.policy_prohibit_public_acces.description: aws-perimeter variant on the EFS file system policy: fails when an Allow statement's principal is exactly the wildcard and no perimeter condition (aws:SourceOwner, SourceAccount, PrincipalOrgID, PrincipalAccount, PrincipalArn, SourceArn with non-wildcard values) restricts it. Such a policy makes the file system accessible to identities outside the account/organization.
aws.c2b.efs.policy_prohibit_public_acces.pass_when: Every wildcard Allow statement is restricted by a perimeter condition key.
aws.c2b.efs.policy_prohibit_public_acces.fail_when: Some wildcard Allow statement has no effective perimeter condition.
aws.c2b.efs.policy_prohibit_public_acces.not_applicable_when: The file system has no file system policy.

aws.c2b.eks.cluster_security_group_prese.description: Reads the EKS DescribeCluster resourcesVpcConfig.clusterSecurityGroupId as evidence of an EKS-created cluster security group ID. It does not inspect security group rules or Kubernetes pod NetworkPolicy. Remediation: Inspect the cluster version, platform, actual security group associations and rules; assess pod NetworkPolicy separately. Do not infer replacement or pod isolation from a missing ID.
aws.c2b.eks.cluster_security_group_prese.pass_when: A plausible sg- ID is observed.
aws.c2b.eks.cluster_security_group_prese.fail_when: No definitive FAIL: a missing, empty or malformed modern ID is UNKNOWN.
aws.c2b.eks.cluster_security_group_prese.not_applicable_when: A provably pre-1.14 or 1.14 pre-eks.3 cluster uses the historical security group model; ambiguous history is UNKNOWN.

aws.c2b.eks.deletion_protection.description: Reads the deletionProtection flag of each EKS cluster and fails only when it is explicitly false (an unreported member is UNKNOWN). Without deletion protection a single DeleteCluster call wipes the control plane and every workload's orchestration state.

aws.c2b.eks.endpoint_not_public.description: aws-perimeter variant: fails any EKS cluster whose resourcesVpcConfig.endpointPublicAccess is true, regardless of publicAccessCidrs restrictions. A public Kubernetes API endpoint is reachable from the Internet, so leaked kubeconfigs or API vulnerabilities can be exploited from anywhere the CIDRs allow.

aws.c2b.eks.endpoint_not_world_open.description: For EKS clusters with endpointPublicAccess true, fails when resourcesVpcConfig.publicAccessCidrs contains the literal 0.0.0.0/0; private-only clusters pass and ::/0 is not considered. An API endpoint open to the whole IPv4 Internet is exposed to credential stuffing and Kubernetes API exploits from any source.
aws.c2b.eks.endpoint_not_world_open.pass_when: The endpoint is private, or the public endpoint CIDRs do not include 0.0.0.0/0.
aws.c2b.eks.endpoint_not_world_open.fail_when: The endpoint is public and publicAccessCidrs includes 0.0.0.0/0.

aws.c2b.eks.secrets_encryption_configure.description: Fails an EKS cluster whose DescribeCluster response has no encryptionConfig entry (omitted means none), regardless of Kubernetes version. Without KMS envelope encryption, Kubernetes Secrets in etcd are protected only by the default EBS-level encryption and cannot be controlled or revoked through a customer KMS key.
aws.c2b.eks.secrets_encryption_configure.pass_when: encryptionConfig contains at least one entry.

aws.c2b.eks.single_security_group.description: Counts resourcesVpcConfig.securityGroupIds (the additional control-plane security groups) of an EKS cluster and fails when more than one is attached. Multiple stacked security groups make the effective allowed traffic to the control plane ENIs hard to review and prone to unintended openings.
aws.c2b.eks.single_security_group.pass_when: Zero or one additional security group is attached.
aws.c2b.eks.single_security_group.fail_when: More than one additional security group is attached.

aws.c2b.eks.version_at_least_1_19.description: Parses the EKS cluster version as (major, minor) and fails when it is below 1.19, the pinned Steampipe floor. Clusters on such old Kubernetes releases are long out of support and miss years of security fixes.
aws.c2b.eks.version_at_least_1_19.pass_when: The Kubernetes version is 1.19 or newer.
aws.c2b.eks.version_at_least_1_19.fail_when: The Kubernetes version is older than 1.19.

aws.c2b.eks.version_at_least_1_28.description: Parses the EKS cluster version as (major, minor) and fails when it is below 1.28, Prowler's default oldest-supported threshold. Clusters below this floor are outside standard support and accumulate unpatched Kubernetes CVEs and incur extended-support costs.
aws.c2b.eks.version_at_least_1_28.pass_when: The Kubernetes version is 1.28 or newer.
aws.c2b.eks.version_at_least_1_28.fail_when: The Kubernetes version is older than 1.28.

aws.c2b.eks.vpc_cni_network_policy.description: Reads the configurationValues JSON of the cluster's managed vpc-cni add-on and fails when enableNetworkPolicy is false (boolean or string); it returns MANUAL when the add-on is absent, the configuration is not a JSON object or the key is unset. Without network policy enforcement, any pod can reach any other pod, so one compromised workload can move laterally across the cluster.
aws.c2b.eks.vpc_cni_network_policy.pass_when: enableNetworkPolicy is true in the vpc-cni add-on configuration.
aws.c2b.eks.vpc_cni_network_policy.not_applicable_when: Never NOT_APPLICABLE; missing managed add-on or unset/unparseable configuration yields MANUAL.

aws.c2b.elasticache.cluster_no_default_s.description: Reads CacheSubnetGroupName of each ElastiCache cache cluster and fails when it is 'default'; a cluster without a subnet group passes. The default subnet group spans the default VPC's subnets, which are typically public, so the cache may land in Internet-routable subnets without deliberate network design.
aws.c2b.elasticache.cluster_no_default_s.pass_when: CacheSubnetGroupName is a non-default name or is omitted.

aws.c2b.elasticache.cluster_public_subne.description: Checks whether any ElastiCache subnet-group subnet has an effective 0.0.0.0/0 route to an internet gateway. A NAT-only route is outbound and is not a public subnet under this ingress criterion. Remediation: Use cache subnets without an internet-gateway default route; inspect security groups and effective ingress separately.
aws.c2b.elasticache.cluster_public_subne.pass_when: No joined subnet has an effective internet-gateway default route.
aws.c2b.elasticache.cluster_public_subne.fail_when: A joined subnet has an effective internet-gateway default route; unresolved joins are UNKNOWN.

aws.c2b.elasticache.cluster_public_subne.description: Prowler variant: resolves the cache cluster's subnet group and fails when any subnet's effective route table (explicit, else VPC main) has 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to an igw- internet gateway; NAT routes are not considered public. Cache nodes in Internet-routed subnets are one security-group or public-IP mistake away from exposing unauthenticated Redis/Memcached ports.
aws.c2b.elasticache.cluster_public_subne.pass_when: No subnet of the cache subnet group has a default route to an internet gateway.
aws.c2b.elasticache.cluster_public_subne.fail_when: Any subnet of the cache subnet group has a 0.0.0.0/0 route to an igw-.

aws.c2b.elasticache.cmk_enabled.description: For each ElastiCache replication group, fails when AtRestEncryptionEnabled is false, when no KmsKeyId is set (default service-managed key), or when the joined KMS key's KeyMetadata.Enabled is false. A disabled key makes snapshots and nodes undecryptable on restart, and default keys cannot be governed by customer key policies.
aws.c2b.elasticache.cmk_enabled.pass_when: At-rest encryption is on with a KmsKeyId whose KMS key is enabled.
aws.c2b.elasticache.cmk_enabled.fail_when: At-rest encryption is off, KmsKeyId is unset, or the referenced KMS key is disabled.

aws.c2b.elasticache.redis_auth_pre6.description: Joins a replication group to its member cache clusters by ReplicationGroupId; if any member runs a Redis engine version below 6.0, the group fails unless AuthTokenEnabled is true (omitted means false). Pre-6.0 Redis has no RBAC, so without an AUTH token any client that reaches the port can read, write or FLUSHALL the cache.
aws.c2b.elasticache.redis_auth_pre6.pass_when: At least one member runs Redis older than 6.0 and AuthTokenEnabled is true.
aws.c2b.elasticache.redis_auth_pre6.fail_when: A member runs Redis older than 6.0 and AuthTokenEnabled is false or omitted.
aws.c2b.elasticache.redis_auth_pre6.not_applicable_when: All member clusters run Redis 6.0 or later (RBAC applies instead).

aws.c2b.elasticache.rg_auto_minor_versio.description: Reads AutoMinorVersionUpgrade on each ElastiCache replication group and fails when it is not true. Without automatic minor upgrades, engine security patches are not applied during maintenance windows and nodes keep running versions with known vulnerabilities.

aws.c2b.elasticache.rg_backup_retention_.description: Checks SnapshotRetentionLimit on an ElastiCache replication group. An omitted value means zero only for a complete native DescribeReplicationGroups response; omission in a partial representation remains UNKNOWN. This evaluates configured snapshot retention, not restore success.
aws.c2b.elasticache.rg_backup_retention_.pass_when: The observed retention limit is at least 15 days.
aws.c2b.elasticache.rg_backup_retention_.fail_when: The observed limit is under 15 days, including zero or a documented default-zero omission in a complete native response.

aws.c2b.elasticache.rg_backup_retention_.description: Prowler variant: reads SnapshotRetentionLimit of each replication group, treating omission as 0 (automatic backups disabled), and fails when it is below 7 days. Groups with no or short automatic snapshots cannot be recovered to a recent point after node loss or data corruption.
aws.c2b.elasticache.rg_backup_retention_.fail_when: SnapshotRetentionLimit is below 7 or omitted (treated as 0).

aws.c2b.elasticache.rg_multi_az.description: Reads the MultiAZ string of each ElastiCache replication group and fails unless it is 'enabled'. Without Multi-AZ, primary node failure or an AZ outage is not met with automatic promotion of a replica in another zone, causing cache downtime and possible data loss.
aws.c2b.elasticache.rg_multi_az.fail_when: MultiAZ is 'disabled' or any value other than 'enabled'.

aws.c2b.elasticbeanstalk.enhanced_health.description: Reads the Elastic Beanstalk environment's aws:elasticbeanstalk:healthreporting:system SystemType option and fails unless one of the returned values is exactly 'enhanced'. With basic health reporting, the environment gets no per-instance OS and application metrics, so degraded or failing instances can go unnoticed.
aws.c2b.elasticbeanstalk.enhanced_health.fail_when: SystemType is set only to other values, such as 'basic'.

aws.c2b.elasticbeanstalk.managed_updates.description: Fails an Elastic Beanstalk environment when no value of the aws:elasticbeanstalk:managedactions ManagedActionsEnabled option equals 'true' (case-insensitive). Without managed actions, platform patch and minor updates are never applied automatically, so instances keep running known-vulnerable platform versions.
aws.c2b.elasticbeanstalk.managed_updates.pass_when: At least one ManagedActionsEnabled option value equals 'true', case insensitively.
aws.c2b.elasticbeanstalk.managed_updates.fail_when: No ManagedActionsEnabled option value equals 'true', including when the option is missing.

aws.c2b.elasticbeanstalk.stream_logs.description: Fails an Elastic Beanstalk environment when the aws:elasticbeanstalk:cloudwatch:logs StreamLogs option has no 'true' value (case-insensitive). If logs are not streamed to CloudWatch Logs, instance and application logs live only on ephemeral instances and are lost on scale-in or replacement, which leaves gaps for incident investigation.
aws.c2b.elasticbeanstalk.stream_logs.pass_when: At least one StreamLogs option value equals 'true', case insensitively.
aws.c2b.elasticbeanstalk.stream_logs.fail_when: No StreamLogs option value equals 'true', including when the option is missing.

aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_http_redirect_default.description: For an application load balancer, lists the HTTP listeners whose DefaultActions contain no action of Type 'redirect' with RedirectConfig.Protocol 'HTTPS', and fails if there are any. Listener rules are not consulted. A plain-HTTP default action serves application traffic unencrypted instead of upgrading clients to TLS.
aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_http_redirect_default.pass_when: Every HTTP listener's default action redirects to HTTPS, or the ALB has no HTTP listeners.
aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_http_redirect_default.fail_when: At least one HTTP listener's default actions lack an HTTPS redirect.
aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_http_redirect_default.not_applicable_when: The load balancer is a network or gateway load balancer.

aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_sg_outbound_rule.description: For an application load balancer, resolves its SecurityGroups in the security group inventory and fails if any of them has an empty IpPermissionsEgress list. An ALB with no security groups also fails. An ALB whose groups have no outbound rules cannot reach its targets or health-check ports, so the service stops working.
aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_sg_outbound_rule.pass_when: The ALB has at least one security group, and every attached group has at least one egress rule.
aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_sg_outbound_rule.fail_when: The ALB has no security groups, or an attached group has no egress rules.
aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_sg_outbound_rule.not_applicable_when: The load balancer is a network or gateway load balancer.

aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_waf_attached.description: For an application load balancer, checks whether its LoadBalancerArn appears in the associated resources of any WAFv2 regional web ACL or any WAF Classic regional web ACL, and fails if it appears in neither. If neither family's associations are collected, the result is UNKNOWN. An ALB without a web ACL gets no layer-7 filtering of injection, bot or volumetric request attacks.
aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_waf_attached.pass_when: The ALB ARN is associated with a WAFv2 or WAF Classic regional web ACL.
aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_waf_attached.fail_when: Association data was collected and no web ACL of either family lists the ALB ARN.
aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_waf_attached.not_applicable_when: The load balancer is a network or gateway load balancer.

aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_wafv2_attached.description: Fails an application load balancer whose LoadBalancerArn is absent from every WAFv2 regional web ACL association; WAF Classic does not count, and uncollected WAFv2 associations produce UNKNOWN. Without a WAFv2 ACL, malicious HTTP requests cannot be screened by its managed rule groups.
aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_wafv2_attached.pass_when: A WAFv2 regional web ACL lists the ALB ARN.
aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_wafv2_attached.fail_when: No WAFv2 web ACL lists the ALB ARN, even if a WAF Classic ACL is attached.
aws.c2b.elbv2.alb_wafv2_attached.not_applicable_when: The load balancer is a network or gateway load balancer.

aws.c2b.elbv2.cross_zone_enabled.description: Fails a network or gateway load balancer whose load_balancing.cross_zone.enabled attribute is 'false'. If the attribute is missing or has any other value, the result is UNKNOWN. When cross-zone balancing is off, each node sends traffic only to targets in its own AZ, so uneven target counts or an AZ losing its targets overloads or blackholes that zone's share.
aws.c2b.elbv2.cross_zone_enabled.not_applicable_when: The load balancer is an application load balancer, which always balances across zones.

aws.c2b.elbv2.has_listeners.description: Fails any ELBv2 load balancer (application, network or gateway) whose collected Listeners list is empty. A load balancer with no listener serves no traffic. It is usually an orphaned resource that still incurs cost and keeps network interfaces and security groups attached.
aws.c2b.elbv2.has_listeners.pass_when: The load balancer has at least one listener.
aws.c2b.elbv2.has_listeners.fail_when: The load balancer has zero listeners.

aws.c2b.elbv2.http_listeners_redirect_ht.description: Checks every HTTP listener's terminal DefaultActions and every collected listener rule action, including its default rule, for an HTTPS redirect. The listener default and default rule must agree. A conditional redirect cannot compensate for a forwarding default; missing rules, malformed actions, or conflicting facts are UNKNOWN.
aws.c2b.elbv2.http_listeners_redirect_ht.pass_when: Every HTTP listener has an HTTPS redirect as its terminal default action and every rule has an HTTPS redirect terminal action; an ALB with no HTTP listeners passes.
aws.c2b.elbv2.http_listeners_redirect_ht.fail_when: A complete HTTP listener default or any complete rule has a non-HTTPS terminal routing action.
aws.c2b.elbv2.http_listeners_redirect_ht.not_applicable_when: The load balancer is not an application load balancer.

aws.c2b.elbv2.insecure_ssl_ciphers.description: Fails an ELBv2 load balancer if any HTTPS listener has an SslPolicy outside the pinned Prowler list of 21 secure ELBSecurityPolicy names (the TLS 1.2+/TLS13, FS-1-2 and 2025-09 PQ policies). TLS and plain listeners are ignored. Older policies allow TLS 1.0/1.1 or weak CBC/RSA ciphers that permit downgrade and decryption attacks on client traffic.
aws.c2b.elbv2.insecure_ssl_ciphers.pass_when: Every HTTPS listener's SslPolicy is in the secure policy list, or there are no HTTPS listeners.
aws.c2b.elbv2.insecure_ssl_ciphers.fail_when: At least one HTTPS listener uses a policy that is not in the list.

aws.c2b.elbv2.internet_facing_open_sg.description: For an internet-facing ELBv2 load balancer, fails if any attached security group has an ingress rule from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 that allows all protocols (-1) or the full TCP range 0-65535. Internal load balancers pass. An internet-facing load balancer behind such a group accepts connections on every port from anywhere, not just its listener ports.
aws.c2b.elbv2.internet_facing_open_sg.pass_when: The scheme is internal, or no attached group allows all traffic or all TCP ports from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.
aws.c2b.elbv2.internet_facing_open_sg.fail_when: The scheme is internet-facing and an attached group has an all-protocol or 0-65535 TCP rule from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0.

aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_certificate_30_da.description: Resolves each ELBv2 listener certificate from ACM NotAfter or IAM server-certificate Expiration and fails if any has fewer than 30 calendar days left at snapshot time; unresolved certificates yield UNKNOWN when none is known to expire. A missed renewal can cause TLS handshake failures and an outage.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_certificate_30_da.pass_when: Every resolved listener certificate has 30 or more days of validity left, and all of them were resolved.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_certificate_30_da.fail_when: Any listener certificate expires in fewer than 30 days, or has already expired.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_certificate_30_da.not_applicable_when: No listener on the load balancer has a certificate attached, for example HTTP/TCP only.

aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_certificate_7_day.description: Uses the same ACM/IAM certificate expiry resolution as the 30-day variant, with a 7-day threshold. It fails if any ELBv2 listener certificate expires within a week of the snapshot clock. This is the near-term signal that clients are about to see expired-certificate errors and that renewal automation has failed.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_certificate_7_day.pass_when: All listener certificates resolve and have at least 7 days remaining.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_certificate_7_day.fail_when: Any listener certificate has fewer than 7 days remaining.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_certificate_7_day.not_applicable_when: No listener on the load balancer carries a certificate.

aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_fips_tls.description: Fails an ELBv2 load balancer if any HTTPS or TLS listener's SslPolicy, split on '-', does not include a 'FIPS' segment. Listeners without TLS are ignored. A non-FIPS policy may negotiate algorithms that are not FIPS 140 validated, which breaks FedRAMP and other FIPS-mandated encryption requirements.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_fips_tls.pass_when: Every HTTPS/TLS listener uses a policy whose name contains a FIPS segment, or there are no HTTPS/TLS listeners.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_fips_tls.fail_when: An HTTPS/TLS listener uses a policy whose name has no FIPS segment.

aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_pqc_tls.description: Fails an ELBv2 load balancer if any HTTPS or TLS listener uses an SslPolicy that is not in Prowler's 11-entry post-quantum list (the 2025-09 *-PQ-* hybrid ML-KEM policies). Without hybrid post-quantum key exchange, recorded TLS sessions are exposed to future 'harvest now, decrypt later' quantum attacks.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_pqc_tls.pass_when: Every HTTPS/TLS listener's policy is a listed PQ policy, or there are no HTTPS/TLS listeners.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listener_pqc_tls.fail_when: Some HTTPS/TLS listener's policy is not in the PQ list.

aws.c2b.elbv2.listeners_acm_certificate.description: For an application or network load balancer, fails if any listener has no certificate ARN containing ':acm:'. A plain HTTP or TCP listener, including an HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect listener, fails, and so does a TLS listener using an IAM server certificate. Certificates not managed in ACM are not renewed automatically and are often uploaded by hand, which raises the risk of expiry and key-handling mistakes.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listeners_acm_certificate.pass_when: Every listener has at least one ACM certificate ARN, or the load balancer has no listeners.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listeners_acm_certificate.fail_when: Some listener has no ACM certificate, for example an HTTP/TCP listener or one with an IAM server certificate.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listeners_acm_certificate.not_applicable_when: The load balancer is a gateway load balancer.

aws.c2b.elbv2.listeners_secure_protocol.description: Requires every listener on an application load balancer to be HTTPS and every listener on a network load balancer to be TLS (Security Hub ELB.18). The check fails and lists each other Protocol:Port, such as HTTP:80 or TCP:443. Listeners that do not terminate TLS carry client traffic in cleartext, or pass it through without the load balancer enforcing encryption.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listeners_secure_protocol.pass_when: All ALB listeners are HTTPS, or all NLB listeners are TLS.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listeners_secure_protocol.fail_when: Any ALB listener is not HTTPS, or any NLB listener is not TLS.
aws.c2b.elbv2.listeners_secure_protocol.not_applicable_when: The load balancer is a gateway load balancer or has no listeners.

aws.c2b.elbv2.nlb_tls_termination.description: Fails a network load balancer when none of its listeners uses Protocol 'TLS'. A single TLS listener passes, even next to plain TCP ones. Without TLS termination the NLB only forwards raw TCP, so encryption depends entirely on each backend and the NLB cannot enforce certificate or policy standards.
aws.c2b.elbv2.nlb_tls_termination.pass_when: At least one NLB listener uses TLS.
aws.c2b.elbv2.nlb_tls_termination.fail_when: No NLB listener uses TLS, for example only TCP/UDP listeners.
aws.c2b.elbv2.nlb_tls_termination.not_applicable_when: The load balancer is an application or gateway load balancer.

aws.c2b.elbv2.not_internet_facing.description: Fails an application or network load balancer whose Scheme is 'internet-facing'. It flags every public entry point, whatever its security groups or WAF. Each internet-facing load balancer adds attack surface, and it needs to be justified and protected by restrictive security groups or WAF.
aws.c2b.elbv2.not_internet_facing.pass_when: Scheme is any value other than 'internet-facing'.
aws.c2b.elbv2.not_internet_facing.not_applicable_when: The load balancer is a gateway load balancer.

aws.c2b.elbv2.recommended_tls_policy.description: Evaluates ALB HTTPS and NLB TLS listeners against the eight reviewed Security Hub ELB.17 approved policy names, including the 2025-09 PQ variants. A known nonapproved policy fails; missing or unreviewed names remain UNKNOWN. This check does not prove a nonapproved policy is necessarily weak or that other listener protocols are unsafe.
aws.c2b.elbv2.recommended_tls_policy.pass_when: Every applicable listener uses one of the eight reviewed ELB.17 policies.
aws.c2b.elbv2.recommended_tls_policy.fail_when: At least one applicable listener uses a known policy outside the ELB.17 approved set.
aws.c2b.elbv2.recommended_tls_policy.not_applicable_when: Gateway load balancers and ALBs without HTTPS or NLBs without TLS listeners.

aws.c2b.emr.block_public_access_enabled.description: Reads the regional EMR block public access configuration and fails when BlockPublicSecurityGroupRules is false. Permitted port exceptions are not examined. With the setting off, EMR clusters can be launched with security groups that allow inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 on any port.

aws.c2b.emr.block_public_access_only_por.description: Fails the regional EMR block public access configuration when BlockPublicSecurityGroupRules is false, or when PermittedPublicSecurityGroupRuleRanges has any range other than exactly 22-22 (Security Hub EMR.2). Having no exception ranges passes. Each extra permitted range allows cluster security groups to expose that port, such as web UIs or Hadoop daemons, to the whole internet.
aws.c2b.emr.block_public_access_only_por.pass_when: Block public access is enabled and the permitted ranges are empty or only 22-22.
aws.c2b.emr.block_public_access_only_por.fail_when: Block public access is disabled, or a permitted range other than 22-22 exists.

aws.c2b.emr.cluster_at_rest_cse_custom.description: Tests the source-specific EMR S3 EncryptionMode CSE-Custom profile. This is an alternative to SSE-KMS, not a universal requirement for every encrypted EMR cluster. Remediation: Select CSE-Custom only where this source profile applies; choose the applicable encryption alternative with the owner before changing a cluster.
aws.c2b.emr.cluster_at_rest_cse_custom.pass_when: The joined security configuration uses CSE-Custom and at-rest encryption is not disabled.
aws.c2b.emr.cluster_at_rest_cse_custom.fail_when: No security configuration, disabled at-rest encryption or another S3 mode; unresolved configuration is UNKNOWN.

aws.c2b.emr.cluster_at_rest_encryption.description: Fails an EMR cluster that has no SecurityConfiguration, or whose joined security configuration does not have EncryptionConfiguration.EnableAtRestEncryption set to true. An unresolvable configuration name gives UNKNOWN. Without at-rest encryption, EMRFS objects in S3 and local or EBS disks on cluster nodes hold processed data in plaintext.
aws.c2b.emr.cluster_at_rest_encryption.pass_when: The joined security configuration has EnableAtRestEncryption true.
aws.c2b.emr.cluster_at_rest_encryption.fail_when: No security configuration is attached, or EnableAtRestEncryption is false or absent.

aws.c2b.emr.cluster_at_rest_sse_kms.description: Tests the source-specific EMR S3 EncryptionMode SSE-KMS profile. This is an alternative to CSE-Custom, not a universal requirement for every encrypted EMR cluster. Remediation: Select SSE-KMS only where this source profile applies; choose the applicable encryption alternative with the owner before changing a cluster.
aws.c2b.emr.cluster_at_rest_sse_kms.pass_when: The joined security configuration uses SSE-KMS and at-rest encryption is not disabled.
aws.c2b.emr.cluster_at_rest_sse_kms.fail_when: No security configuration, disabled at-rest encryption or another S3 mode; unresolved configuration is UNKNOWN.

aws.c2b.emr.cluster_in_transit_encryptio.description: Fails an EMR cluster with no SecurityConfiguration, or one whose joined configuration does not set EnableInTransitEncryption to true. An unresolved name gives UNKNOWN. Without in-transit TLS, shuffle traffic, Spark/Tez RPC and EMRFS S3 requests between nodes can be read or tampered with on the VPC network.
aws.c2b.emr.cluster_in_transit_encryptio.pass_when: The joined configuration has EnableInTransitEncryption true.
aws.c2b.emr.cluster_in_transit_encryptio.fail_when: No security configuration is attached, or EnableInTransitEncryption is not true.

aws.c2b.emr.cluster_kerberos_enabled.description: Uses the DescribeCluster detail (Cluster.Id proves it was read) and fails when KerberosAttributes is absent, which means the cluster was launched without Kerberos authentication. Without Kerberos, Hadoop services and users on the cluster are not strongly authenticated, so anyone with network access can impersonate users to YARN, HDFS or Hive.
aws.c2b.emr.cluster_kerberos_enabled.pass_when: KerberosAttributes is present on the cluster.

aws.c2b.emr.cluster_local_disk_cmk.description: Fails an EMR cluster when there is no security configuration, when AtRestEncryptionConfiguration.LocalDiskEncryptionConfiguration is missing, or when its EncryptionKeyProviderType is not 'Custom'. The AwsKms provider fails too. Node instance-store and EBS volumes are then not encrypted with the custom key provider that the policy requires.
aws.c2b.emr.cluster_local_disk_cmk.fail_when: There is no security configuration or no local disk configuration, or the provider type is AwsKms or anything other than Custom.

aws.c2b.emr.cluster_local_disk_encryptio.description: Passes an EMR cluster only when its joined security configuration has EnableAtRestEncryption true and also defines AtRestEncryptionConfiguration.LocalDiskEncryptionConfiguration. A missing configuration or either part missing fails. Otherwise HDFS blocks, shuffle spill and temporary data on node disks stay unencrypted, even when S3 encryption is set.
aws.c2b.emr.cluster_local_disk_encryptio.pass_when: EnableAtRestEncryption is true and a LocalDiskEncryptionConfiguration is present.
aws.c2b.emr.cluster_local_disk_encryptio.fail_when: There is no security configuration, at-rest encryption is not true, or there is no local disk encryption configuration.

aws.c2b.emr.cluster_not_publicly_accessi.description: For a non-terminated EMR cluster with public Amazon master DNS, fails if a managed or additional primary or core/task security group admits all protocols or the full 0-65535 port range from a public CIDR. Such ingress can expose Hadoop or Spark service ports and web interfaces to the Internet.
